Question: Why are most films based on video games bad?
Answer: *there is a spoiler telling the end of The Last of Us Because the gameplay is often a huge part of what makes a game fun. Let’s pick the Legend of Zelda serie as an example. Link, the protagonist, is totally silent (well, he does scream “HAAA” though), but the player still get immersed. Could you imagine a movie in which the main character don’t talk? It does exist, but it has to be amazingly great to still be an interesting movie. However, for video games, it’s very common. It’s because the scenario can be way simplier than a movie’s scenario before it gets interesting. Movies like Lara Croft and Assassin’s Creed were fails because these games rely too much on you executing the actions to be well adapted. In a movie, the spectator is passive. He watches other characters. In a video game, the player is active. When I watch a movie, I have no power to decide if a character dies or not. In video games, if I fail and the protagonist dies, it’s my fault. Therefore, it is way more stressful. I remember playing INSIDE and feeling so much that I had to save that little guy because the death scenes were so gruesome and I would then feel very guilty. Let’s also pick The Last of Us as another example. The story is amazing and I’m sure it could be an amazing movie too, but it still wouldn’t be as enjoyable as the game for most people. In some scenes, the fact I was the one controlling Joel made it way better (shooting scenes, the subway underground scene, the flooded basement scene, the gymnase scene). SPOILER And what about the end? I felt so shitty when I killed these nurses and realized I could have spared them. So I got much more immersed than if I would simply have watched a character doing it. Now, I did it. In Until Dawn, at some point, when a monster is very close to you, you have to hold stiff the controller. If you move to much, you die. Can you imagine a movie making you participate that much? You can even kill characters and the story continues anyway, so the story depends on your performance. The lenght is also an important factor although TV shows are now a good solution to that problem. So the answer is mainly because in a video game, a huge part of the fun is the player being directly involved in the story instead of just being passive and looking at it. Just take a look at games made by TellTale studio. The player actually have little control on the story and there aren’t that much gameplay, so when they fail to present amazing scenarios, the games get bad reviews. You want to sell a cheap scenario? Offer great game mecanisms. If you don’t, it’s just boring. Like a bad movie.

Question: What is the difference between "bien" and "bon" in French?
Answer: “bon/mauvais” are adjectives: they add information about nouns → “un bon ami”, “une mauvaise voiture”… We also use them to talk about a talent, or the lack of a talent: “Je suis bon à la flûte.”, “Je suis mauvaise au piano.”… We also use them to talk about the taste or something you can smell: “La tarte est bonne.”, “Ce parfum a une mauvaise odeur.”… → In that situation, they can be adverbs (so they are invariable) if we use them to change the verbs “goûter” (to taste) and “sentir” (to smell): “Elle goûte bon.” or “Ils sentent mauvais.” With the verb “être” (to be), we use them to say that we like something quite a lot: “Ce film est bon.”, “Cette chanson est mauvaise.”… “bien/mal” are adverbs: they add information about verbs → “Ils chantent mal.”, “Tu parles bien.”… We also use them to talk about the morality or the “legal state” of something: “Voler est mal.”, “Aider les personnes âgées est bien.”… With the verb “être” (to be), we use “bien” (but not “mal”) to say we kind of like something, that is was only okay: “Ce film est bien.”, “Cette chanson est bien.”… “bien” is also an adverb that means “a lot” → “Il mange bien trop.”, “Tu es bien content!”…

Question: How is antithesis effective?
Answer: An antithesis can be used to show the “wide range” of something. An antithesis can be use to create an odd figures. Horror use that technique a lot, and the result often actually transcends the two initial images. → This actually explains why a lot of monster, in horror, are kids, especially little girls. We see them as innocent and pure and to put them in a horrific context is very odd, therefore creates discomfort, which helps to make horror more effective. There are other effects an antithesis can creates, it may depend on the situation. One famous French antithesis is from Raymond Queneau: “Zazie se tient de grands discours avec sa petite voix intérieure.” It means: “The small voice in Zazie’s head makes big discourses.” In that situation, it shows that Zazie is a very humble person, but that she has big ambitions and dreams. It’s the antithesis that helps understand that.

Question: Why does French from France or from Paris sound so much better than French made in Quebec?
Answer: This is a very subjective question so you’re the one who can truly know. The truth is, as many people already said: there isn’t a “good” or a “bad” French. But as much as I disagree with you, I can try to guide you a little bit. Also, there are more than one French accent in France, so I’ll answer talking about a “standard” Parisian French (the one you’ll hear watching the news). In France, people tend to pronounce more than in Québec. They pronounce every syllable, which isn’t true in Québec. “Il ne vient plus.” in France will sound “Y vient pu” in Québec. The mouth muscles are also more relaxed while speaking the French from Québec. It is especially true when we pronounce the letter “t” in front of the letter “i” and “u”, because the “t” is then pronounced “ts”. The mouth has less often a “O” shape. In short, the French enunciate more. But we have an expression here to talk about people who don’t enunciate enough: “That person talks as if she/he had a hot potato in her/his mouth.” And I want to finish by saying that I love the French spoken here, in Québec. <3
